newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat falls in Milan despite new car scheme.
newsitem.headline: Fiat falls in Milan despite new car scheme.

text.p: Fiat closed lower on the Milan stock exchange in a market which traders said had overrated the effects on the Turin car giant of a government bonus scheme for motorists to trade in old cars for new to boost sales.
Fiat stock ended 2.97 percent down at 4,250 lire against a range of 4,235/4,410 lire on Tuesday in volume of just over seven million shares. The Bourse was a touch firmer overall.
"The positive effects of incentives on Fiat's net capitalisation will be of the order of one to two percent, almost nothing," said analyst Alberto Rolla at brokers Pasfin.

He estimated the scheme would generate extra Fiat car sales of between 60,000 and 110,000 this year. A Fiat executive said earlier he saw an extra 150,000 sales due to the scheme which will operate until end-September.

The government said motorists who traded in cars over 10-years old would get a bonus of 1.5 million lire for vehicles with engines of less than 1,300 cc and up to two million lire for cars with larger engines. Car makers will have to match each bonus on offer with a similar discount.
Rolla said, "The incentives, which will sustain demand of the smaller-to-medium model range, will however help Fiat keep its domestic market share (of some 44 percent)."
Gianluca Pediconi of Milla brokers forecast Fiat's earnings per share in 1997 rising to 327 lire due to the incentives scheme.

"Fiat should increase sales by 150,000 cars, with an increase in turnover of six to eight percent. But we will not see the same growth in margins which will be impacted by reduced recourse to temporary lay-offs and the fact that demand will focus more on the lower-to-medium model range."
He saw a "correct" price for Fiat shares of 4,250/4,300 lire.
"We are expecting an improvement in results, but not as an effect of the incentives scheme," said one analyst who declined to be named. "I think the company is fully valued at current price levels."
